HL Financial Services LLC trimmed its stake in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 1.3% during the fourth quarter, according to its most recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The firm owned 1,445,940 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 19,610 shares during the quarter. Apple comprises 4.7% of HL Financial Services LLC’s portfolio, making the stock its 3rd largest position. HL Financial Services LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $244,698,000 as of its most recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Other institutional investors also recently made changes to their positions in the company. Gilbert & Cook Inc. grew its holdings in Apple by 5.3% in the 4th quarter. Gilbert & Cook Inc. now owns 6,477 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $1,096,000 after buying an additional 326 shares in the last quarter. GenWealth Group Inc. bought a new position in Apple in the 4th quarter worth approximately $519,000. Iberiabank Corp grew its holdings in Apple by 14.5% in the 4th quarter. Iberiabank Corp now owns 54,475 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $9,328,000 after buying an additional 6,913 shares in the last quarter. Trillium Asset Management LLC grew its holdings in Apple by 11.7% in the 4th quarter. Trillium Asset Management LLC now owns 114,193 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $19,325,000 after buying an additional 11,958 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Parametrica Management Ltd bought a new position in Apple in the 4th quarter worth approximately $328,000. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 60.93% of the company’s stock. In other Apple news, insider Chris Kondo sold 4,867 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction dated Wednesday, May 16th. The stock was sold at an average price of $187.00, for a total transaction of $910,129.00. Following the transaction, the insider now directly owns 8,433 shares in the company, valued at $1,576,971. The transaction was disclosed in a filing with the SEC, which is available through this link . Also, COO Jeffrey E. Williams sold 15,653 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction dated Tuesday, May 8th. The shares were sold at an average price of $185.18, for a total value of $2,898,622.54. Following the transaction, the chief operating officer now owns 168,181 shares in the company, valued at $31,143,757.58. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last 90 days, insiders have sold 219,736 shares of company stock worth $38,403,373. Corporate insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock. NASDAQ AAPL opened at $186.31 on Friday. Apple has a fifty-two week low of $142.20 and a fifty-two week high of $190.37. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80, a quick ratio of 1.37 and a current ratio of 1.46. The stock has a market cap of $948.79 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 20.23, a P/E/G ratio of 1.39 and a beta of 1.26.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last posted its earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share for the quarter, beating the Thomson Reuters’ consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The company had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. During the same period last year, the company earned $2.10 earnings per share. The business’s revenue was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.43 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
Apple declared that its board has authorized a stock buyback plan on Tuesday, May 1st that authorizes the company to buyback $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This buyback authorization authorizes the iPhone maker to repurchase up to 11.9% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock buyback plans are usually an indication that the company’s board of directors believes its shares are undervalued.
The business also recently announced a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, May 17th. Shareholders of record on Monday, May 14th were issued a dividend of $0.73 per share. This is a positive change from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.57%. The ex-dividend date was Friday, May 11th. Apple’s dividend payout ratio (DPR) is 31.70%.
A number of equities analysts recently issued reports on the company. BidaskClub raised Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a report on Wednesday, May 9th. Zacks Investment Research raised Apple from a “sell” rating to a “hold” rating in a report on Thursday, May 3rd. ValuEngine raised Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a report on Wednesday, May 2nd. Morningstar set a $175.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a report on Wednesday, May 2nd. Finally, Atlantic Securities reissued a “neutral” rating and issued a $185.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a report on Wednesday, May 2nd. One analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have issued a hold rating, thirty-three have issued a buy rating and two have assigned a strong buy rating to the company. The company has a consensus rating of “Buy” and a consensus target price of $204.00.
About Apple
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide. The company also sells related software, services, accessories, networking solutions, and third-party digital content and applications.
